title: Prove source gauges cannot help before the third use (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with exact finite corroboration. In ADD-once bipartite dyadic shears, every fully restored source gauge on a source used at most twice can be erased without increasing scalar allowance, regardless of simultaneous target gauges or ADD order. The coupled optimum therefore equals Dugongue's target-only interval formula from #4518. This answers the low-use part of its second Open next question.

```text
Sources with at most two uses: coupled optimum = target-only optimum
Equal-coefficient d-leaf star: d c(o) + 2 min(d,2)|v|
First strict example, three half-weight ADDs: 30 -> 28 scalar units
```

The threshold is sharp. The proof covers arbitrary finite integer gauge paths and arbitrary dirty initial data, charges every entry/return SCALE, and supplies the matching inverse-dual interface. The elementary shared-factor star construction and classical Levi identity are credited; the new result is the source-elimination theorem and exact threshold under this schedule contract. No new kappa is claimed.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit David Ganz / Dugongue's #4518 tariff, target-only theorem and question, its #4502/#4505/native lineage, Ali Romman's #5783/#5824/#5830 fixed-graph optimization, and Richard Hoekstra's #1235 phase-gauge tour work. No predecessor scientific suite was replayed or audited.

## Evidence

- Before: #4518's interval optimum restricts all source gauges to zero and leaves coupled paths open. After: the same optimum is proved for the enlarged class whenever source use is at most two; a fully restored degree-three star attains the exact smaller cost.
- A separate bounded Dijkstra implementation checks all 256 two-source/two-target absent-or-valuation lists, every ADD order and gauge states in {-1,0,1}. Both coupled and source-fixed minima match the interval formula. The written proof, rather than the finite gauge box, establishes the unbounded conclusion.
- 81 prescribed gauge-path fixtures, 18 star and 18 reversed-star shortest-path problems, 51 further exact star witnesses, full arbitrary-input matrix/inverse-dual endpoints, and eight rejecting controls pass in normal and optimized modes. Reversed stars exercise profitable target movement while every source is low-use.
- CPython 3.12.15, standard library only. Warning-strict direct checks pass in 1.007 s and 0.953 s; the registered wrapper runs both commands and passes in 2.099 s. Each registered command is below its 120 s timeout. These are check durations, not a speed comparison.
- Metadata/pins, committed bytes, source ancestry and executable modes pass at `00675f5c3e011bc0627d5e1ea381ed30f922eb0c`. The official eight-file export passes integrity and declared-input coverage; normal and optimized replays pass outside Git with an empty executable PATH. A generated stdout receipt binds the six package files by SHA256.

From the worktree/repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -X dev -I -B research/low-use-source-gauges/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -X dev -I -O -B research/low-use-source-gauges/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/low-use-source-gauges
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/low-use-source-gauges --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Any CPython 3.12 executable can replace that path. Direct replay prints `PASS_LOW_USE_SOURCE_GAUGES no_new_kappa`; registered replay prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Sparse checkouts should materialize `research/levi-adaptive-gauges` first. SOURCES.json pins the cited mathematical inputs and historical task/selected provenance. The cheap selected-baseline binding orientation also passes after materializing its closure.

## Limitations

The theorem fixes the list of ADD contributions, allows only disjoint pure source and target roles and positive power-of-two gauge scales, uses #4518's scalar tariff, and restores every gauge. It does not optimize general circuits, coalescing, borrowing, source writes, target reads, non-diagonal changes or unreturned gauges. No actual P104 word or paid/target histogram is changed.

Native implementation, physical precision/tape costs, rounded arithmetic, caller integration and complete multiplication remain outside this result. All five selected framework assumptions remain. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Selected cold replay, predecessor scientific suites, Lean and Docker were not run. Ruff is unavailable locally; warning-strict Python checks pass. The README records the bounded CPython allocation deviation under Power of Ten.

## Open next questions

Which sources with at least three uses in one named complete native window admit a profitable restored gauge after the surrounding interfaces are charged? Extract one ADD-once bipartite window, retain its target-only optimum and prune its low-use sources by this theorem. The emitted-window, caller, native and precision/tape contracts are the blockers to adoption. This contribution stops at the first sharp threshold result.

## Related open work

- #6121 optimizes ADD/SCALE logical defect guards on the historical THREE-base suffix ledger. This contribution optimizes a different quantity, scalar allowance in bipartite gauge schedules, and supplies no new defect budget or native-word installation.
- #6116 resynthesizes the selected P104 scalar prefix by changing its arithmetic word. This theorem fixes the ADD list and prices source/target representation paths; its 28/30 star is not a cost claim for that complete prefix.

Main, merged-work, open-PR, recent account, Discussion and local-claim searches were refreshed before the commit. No competing claim on this source-use threshold was found. Cached local-note coverage is sparse and unpublished work is not excluded. No global literature-priority claim is made.

Completion refresh inspected all eleven other open account PRs created since the advance CLAIM: #6121, #6122, #6123, #6124, #6125, #6126, #6127, #6128, #6129, #6131 and #6132. #6121 concerns the same historical native family and is distinguished above. The others concern query capacity, centre kernels, sampler tables and reversal, leaf tariffs and tails, Gaussian conditioning/concentration, rounded Walsh error and ADDRESS characters. None supplies a competing coupled dyadic source-gauge optimum or a value for this star. No extra computations were run to compare their results.

Advance claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19241957

## CI notes

The failure is inherited from canonical main `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`, the PR6030 kappa-admission commit pushed with `[skip ci]`. It updated the selected record without matching the required documentation format/navigation. The failed-job log confirms exactly these two onboarding failures:

- `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record` expects `make frontier6030-verify` in `docs/ci.md`, which still describes selected PR5599 and `make frontier5599-verify`.

The log reports 678 tests, two failures and 23 skips. [PR #6120's run 40691776027](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40691776027) fails the same two tests, confirmed from its failed-job log. This package did not cause either failure. Incidental negative-fixture diagnostic text is not counted as another test failure.

**A maintainer re-run is required after main's documentation is fixed.** No branch push, documentation fix or CI re-run was performed for this blocker. Local normal/optimized, registered, committed-source and portable-export checks remain passing evidence; hosted replay remains uncertified.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated.
